newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Arrest order lifted on S.African oil rig.
newsitem.headline: Arrest order lifted on S.African oil rig.

text.p: South Africa's Soekor (Pty) Ltd said on Friday its oil pumping rig Orca had been released from an arrest order, allowing it to start sea trials as soon as the weather allowed.
Orca was due to have begun sea trials last Monday but could not leave Simonstown harbour, where it had undergone an extensive refit, because of a legal dispute between contractors.

"Orca has been released from its arrest by the sheriff of Simonstown after its main contractor, Schlumberger Logelco Inc, provided the necessary security to offset the Babcock (subcontractor) claims for improvements made to the Orca," Soekor said in a statement on Friday.
"The Orca is waiting for more favourable weather and sea conditions prior to moving from the quayside for the completion of the sea trials."

The rig was "arrested" late on Monday by the sheriff's office due to a 31 million rand debt owed by contractor Schlumberger, who has been refurbishing the rig, to local sub-contractor Babcock Construction .
Soekor said last week before the court order that Orca should be on site and pumping 20,000 BPD from the Oribi field off Mossel Bay at the end of March.
